# Proposal: Guided AI GRC Build for Tamarack Instruments

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel, Tamarack Instruments
**Program:** Guided AI GRC Build, AI Governance Academy
**Basis:** Discovery call notes of 6 October 2026
**Decision requested by:** 15 December 2026

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. It is headquartered in the Netherlands and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States, with about 1,100 staff. The Client is at the piloting stage of AI maturity and has three AI use cases:

- **Deployed:** a customer service chatbot on the support portal.
- **Piloting:** AI visual inspection on the German production line.
- **Planned:** AI sales forecasting next year.

A June 2026 internal audit finding recorded that the Client has no inventory of AI systems. The regulatory drivers are the EU AI Act and GDPR. The Client already operates an ISO/IEC 27001 information security management system and an ISO 9001 quality management system. It intends to begin ISO/IEC 42001 work next year, although that start date is not fixed.

Your stated objective is clear: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027." Three constraints shape the build:

- Budget is approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.
- Customer data must stay in the EU.
- The German works council must be consulted before anything touches production staff.

The program fits within the approved budget. If the build starts in early January 2027, it would complete within Q1 2027, ahead of the stated Q2 2027 production target. The start date is a decision for the Client.

## 2. Why a Guided Build Rather Than Consulting Delivery

A consulting engagement typically hands over a finished set of documents. A guided build works differently. Your own team builds the management system during the twelve weeks with weekly coaching, so the people who will operate it understand why each element exists and can run it when the program ends.

This matters for Tamarack for three reasons:

1. **Audit response.** The internal audit finding concerns an operational gap, not a missing document. Closing it depends on an inventory that the Client keeps current.
2. **Future certification work.** ISO/IEC 42001 work planned for next year will rely on evidence produced by people inside the organization.
3. **Accountability.** Our principles of Slow AI, Informed Intent and Final Liability rests with the Human place accountability with the Client's own decision makers rather than with an outside adviser.

The build uses two open frameworks:

- **GRC Workbook** (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook) for governance artifacts.
- **Slow AI Kitchen** (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen) for governed workflows and human oversight.

Board-level reporting can draw on **AI Governance for Boards** (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards).

## 3. The Twelve-Week Spine, Tailored to Tamarack

**Inventory sequencing.** The inventory begins with the customer service chatbot because it is the only system recorded as deployed and it faces customers. Visual inspection enters second because it is in pilot with a stated Q2 2027 production target, which makes its classification and assessment time-critical. Sales forecasting is registered as a planned system so that governance applies before it is built.

**ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO 9001 integration.** The build will attach to the Client's existing ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO 9001 structures rather than create parallel ones. The specific artifacts each week attaches to are not stated in the Profile Block, so they appear as `Unknown` below until they are identified at Week 1.

**ISO/IEC 42001 mapping.** These mappings describe readiness themes only. They are not a certification outcome.

| Week | Tamarack focus | ISO/IEC 42001 readiness theme | ISMS / QMS integration point |
|---|---|---|---|
| W1 | Mobilization, charter and roles. Confirm the scope and response approach for the audit finding. | Context of the organization; leadership | Unknown |
| W2 | AI system inventory: chatbot, then visual inspection, then sales forecasting as planned | Context; AI system scope | Unknown |
| W3 | Classification and risk methodology, including EU AI Act classification of each system (confirm with external counsel) | Planning; risk criteria | Unknown |
| W4 | Risk and impact assessments for the chatbot and visual inspection, including whether GDPR data protection impact assessment duties apply (confirm with external counsel) | AI risk assessment; AI system impact assessment | Unknown |
| W5 | Risk register and treatment | Risk treatment | Unknown |
| W6 | Core policy set and mid-point steering | AI policy; leadership | Unknown |
| W7 | Operating procedures and lifecycle governance, including the pilot-to-production gate for visual inspection | Operation; AI system life cycle | Unknown |
| W8 | Vendor and supplier governance, including the EU customer data residency requirement; evidence collection begins | Third-party and supplier relationships | Unknown |
| W9 | Governed workflows and human oversight using Slow AI Kitchen | Operation; human oversight | Unknown |
| W10 | Testing, evaluation and monitoring | Performance evaluation | Unknown |
| W11 | Incident response, change management and evidence review | Improvement; operational control | Unknown |
| W12 | Audit readiness review, evidence walkthrough and closing steering | Internal audit readiness; management review | Unknown |

Three items require early attention:

- **Supplier status.** Whether the chatbot or the visual inspection system is supplied by a vendor is `Unknown`.
- **EU data residency.** Whether customer data currently stays in the EU for each system is `Unknown`. Both points will be established at W2.
- **Works council consultation.** Whether any W2 through W10 activity touches production staff is `Unknown`. If it does, works council consultation must be scheduled before that activity begins. Confirm the scope and timing of consultation with external counsel.

## 4. Contracted Outcome: Minimum Viable AIMS at Week 12

The contracted outcome is a minimum viable Artificial Intelligence Management System with six elements:

1. An adopted charter.
2. A populated inventory.
3. An operating risk register.
4. An adopted core policy set.
5. At least two governed AI workflows in production use.
6. Evidence collection running for at least four weeks.

**Delivery risk for element 5.** Only the chatbot is recorded as deployed. Visual inspection is targeted for production in Q2 2027, which may fall after Week 12. The second governed workflow in production use is therefore `Unknown` and must be agreed at the Week 1 steering checkpoint.

## 5. Client Team Commitment

The standing build team is drawn from the roles below. The figures are **estimates** of average weekly hours, including the workshop, coaching and asynchronous work. Actual effort will vary by week.

| Role | Estimated hours per week | Estimated peak weeks |
|---|---|---|
| General Counsel (Sponsor) | 3 to 4 | W1, W3, W6, W12 |
| CISO | 4 to 5 | W4, W8, W11 |
| Head of Quality | 4 to 5 | W7, W10, W11 |
| Head of Data | 5 to 6 | W2, W4, W9, W10 |
| German plant manager | 2 to 4 | W2, W4, W7, W9 |
| Internal auditor (each of two) | 2 to 3 | W5, W11, W12 |

## 6. Steering Cadence

Executive steering checkpoints take place at Weeks 1, 6 and 12:

- **Week 1:** confirms scope, the team, delivery risks and the second production workflow.
- **Week 6:** reviews spine status and decides any scope changes.
- **Week 12:** reviews the minimum viable AIMS against the six-element definition.

Steering membership beyond the Sponsor is `Unknown` and will be confirmed at mobilization.

## 7. Logistics and Price

- **Duration:** 12 weeks.
- **Weekly cadence:** one live virtual workshop, one coaching session and structured asynchronous implementation between sessions.
- **Scheduling:** session times across the Client's operating jurisdictions are `Unknown` and will be agreed at mobilization.
- **Price:** US$60,000, within the approved budget of up to US$80,000.
- **Commercial terms:** payment terms are `Unknown`. Contract terms carry legal effect; confirm with external counsel.

## 8. Next Step

We propose a 45-minute confirmation call with you before 15 December 2026 to settle four points:

1. The program start date.
2. The second governed AI workflow targeted for production use by Week 12.
3. Steering membership.
4. The ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO 9001 artifacts the build will attach to.

On your approval, mobilization materials for Week 1 will follow.
